ai.description: This slender viper reaches 75–100 cm. It is bright green with a yellow venter and a distinct white lateral stripe. A triangular head and vertical pupils are key diagnostic features.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Trimeresurus gramineus* is the presence of a distinct, thin white or yellow ventrolateral stripe running along the entire body length.
ai.habitat: The Common Bamboo Viper inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often residing in bamboo thickets and shrubs at elevations up to 2,000 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Common Bamboo Viper is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless on branches to ambush small prey like frogs, lizards, and rodents that pass within its strike range.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus gramineus* is viviparous, typically producing a litter of 6–10 young. Breeding generally occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Bamboo Viper is primarily found in the Western Ghats and parts of southern India, typically inhabiting forests at elevations from sea level up to 2,000 meters.
